      "title": "Multiple crypto providers are now silently selected, with no tie-break for equal orders",
      "body": "CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now sorts all discovered CryptoProvider services and returns the first one instead of failing when multiple services are present. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so if more than one is accidentally on the classpath the winner is determined only by ServiceLoader/classpath order. In addition, all providers are instantiated before selection, so constructors that register JCA security providers run even for ignored providers. This can silently select a non-FIPS provider in a FIPS deployment or leave multiple security providers registered, breaking the previous fail-fast guarantee and creating a security/compliance risk."
    },

      "title": "New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations",
      "body": "CryptoProvider is a public interface, but order() was added as an abstract method. Existing implementations outside this repository, or older modules compiled against the previous interface, will fail to compile and may fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when ServiceLoader sorting invokes order(). A default method would preserve compatibility."
    },

      "file": "authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java",

      "category": "security",
      "title": "Oversized ECDSA integers are truncated instead of rejected",
      "body": "In AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA converter, integerToBytes truncates any BigInteger whose byte array is longer than qLength by copying only the last qLength bytes. For a valid ECDSA signature, r and s must not be larger than the coordinate size, allowing at most one leading zero byte. Silently truncating oversized DER integers accepts malformed signatures and changes the numeric value, which can create signature malleability or unexpected verification behavior. The method should reject values that do not fit and should also reject negative integers."
    },

      "file": "authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java",
      "line": 57,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "ASN.1 sequence parsing is too lenient and can ignore malformed or trailing data",
      "body": "ASN1Decoder.readSequence does not validate that the declared SEQUENCE length is exactly consumed. If a child TLV is longer than the remaining sequence length, the remaining length becomes negative and parsing stops without error. If trailing bytes exist after the SEQUENCE, they are ignored because asn1derToConcatenatedRS only reads the first sequence. This lenient DER parsing can accept malformed or appended signature bytes. It should reject non-zero remaining length, child lengths that exceed the sequence, and unconsumed trailing input."
    },

      "title": "Indefinite-length ASN.1 values can cause NegativeArraySizeException",
      "body": "ASN1Decoder.readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding, but callers do not handle it. readInteger passes that -1 to read(int), which executes new byte[-1] and throws NegativeArraySizeException rather than IOException. readSequence treats -1 as an empty sequence. DER signatures must use definite length, so indefinite length should be rejected explicitly."
    },

      "body": "AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()), which may be the default JDK keystore provider and has no relation to BouncyCastle. The CryptoProvider contract says this method returns the BouncyCastle security provider. If any caller uses the returned provider expecting BouncyCastle services, it can pick the wrong provider or fail. If this minimal provider has no BouncyCastle provider, it should return null or avoid exposing an incorrect provider."
    },

A shorter array causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, while a longer array silently ignores trailing bytes. Cryptographic conversion should require the exact expected length to avoid crashes and malformed-signature acceptance."
    },
    {
      "file": "authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java",
      "line": 42,

      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "ECDSA conversion test does not use the expected curves or verify signatures",
      "body": "ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a default EC key pair and only asserts that concatenated R/S bytes are stable across conversion. It does not initialize the generator with the curves associated with ES256, ES384, and ES512, does not verify the reconstructed DER signature with the public key, and does not cover edge cases such as r/s values with the high bit set, leading zeros, extreme values, or malformed DER. This leaves the custom ASN.1 conversion insufficiently tested."
    }

findings.title: Multiple crypto providers are now silently selected, with no tie-break for equal orders
findings.body: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now sorts all discovered CryptoProvider services and returns the first one instead of failing when multiple services are present. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so if more than one is accidentally on the classpath the winner is determined only by ServiceLoader/classpath order. In addition, all providers are instantiated before selection, so constructors that register JCA security providers run even for ignored providers. This can silently select a non-FIPS provider in a FIPS deployment or leave multiple security providers registered, breaking the previous fail-fast guarantee and creating a security/compliance risk.

findings.title: New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public interface, but order() was added as an abstract method. Existing implementations outside this repository, or older modules compiled against the previous interface, will fail to compile and may fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when ServiceLoader sorting invokes order(). A default method would preserve compatibility.

findings.title: Oversized ECDSA integers are truncated instead of rejected
findings.body: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA converter, integerToBytes truncates any BigInteger whose byte array is longer than qLength by copying only the last qLength bytes. For a valid ECDSA signature, r and s must not be larger than the coordinate size, allowing at most one leading zero byte. Silently truncating oversized DER integers accepts malformed signatures and changes the numeric value, which can create signature malleability or unexpected verification behavior. The method should reject values that do not fit and should also reject negative integers.

findings.title: ASN.1 sequence parsing is too lenient and can ignore malformed or trailing data
findings.body: ASN1Decoder.readSequence does not validate that the declared SEQUENCE length is exactly consumed. If a child TLV is longer than the remaining sequence length, the remaining length becomes negative and parsing stops without error. If trailing bytes exist after the SEQUENCE, they are ignored because asn1derToConcatenatedRS only reads the first sequence. This lenient DER parsing can accept malformed or appended signature bytes. It should reject non-zero remaining length, child lengths that exceed the sequence, and unconsumed trailing input.

findings.title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 values can cause NegativeArraySizeException
findings.body: ASN1Decoder.readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding, but callers do not handle it. readInteger passes that -1 to read(int), which executes new byte[-1] and throws NegativeArraySizeException rather than IOException. readSequence treats -1 as an empty sequence. DER signatures must use definite length, so indefinite length should be rejected explicitly.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated JCA provider
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()), which may be the default JDK keystore provider and has no relation to BouncyCastle. The CryptoProvider contract says this method returns the BouncyCastle security provider. If any caller uses the returned provider expecting BouncyCastle services, it can pick the wrong provider or fail. If this minimal provider has no BouncyCastle provider, it should return null or avoid exposing an incorrect provider.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate input signature length
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the supplied concatenated signature has exactly signLength bytes. It does not validate signature.length before System.arraycopy. A shorter array causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, while a longer array silently ignores trailing bytes. Cryptographic conversion should require the exact expected length to avoid crashes and malformed-signature acceptance.

findings.title: ECDSA conversion test does not use the expected curves or verify signatures
findings.body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a default EC key pair and only asserts that concatenated R/S bytes are stable across conversion. It does not initialize the generator with the curves associated with ES256, ES384, and ES512, does not verify the reconstructed DER signature with the public key, and does not cover edge cases such as r/s values with the high bit set, leading zeros, extreme values, or malformed DER. This leaves the custom ASN.1 conversion insufficiently tested.
